### Technical Interview 1 | Difficulty: Medium

The first technical round focused mainly on DSA.

One reported problem was:

**Maximum of minimum for every window size k**

The discussion also covered the optimization from a brute-force approach to an efficient solution using a suitable data structure.

Another type of question involved designing a data structure supporting:

* `addElement()`
* `deleteElement()`
* `getRandomElement()`

with **O(1)** expected time.

---

### Technical Interview 2 | Difficulty: Medium

The next round included additional DSA and problem-solving questions.

A common pattern reported in Flipkart interviews is a **tree-based problem**, where the interviewer gives a tree and asks you to identify or calculate nodes satisfying a particular condition.

The discussion can then move into recursion, traversal, complexity, and possible optimizations.

There were also questions around projects, technologies used, and my contribution to the project.

---

### Final Discussion | Difficulty: Easy-Medium

The final discussion was more conversational and included questions about my background, projects, teamwork, and career interests.

The overall interview was strongly focused on explaining the reasoning behind the solution rather than simply writing code.

#### Interview Experience at Flipkart for SDE1
##### Background: 
B.Tech in CSE, Tier 2 college. 2023 Grad.
Previously SDE intern at Amazon (6 months). 

Feb/March 2024
Applied off campus, don't really remember when or where, because I had sent out hundreds (maybe thousands) of applications over a few months. No referral.
I got an email saying I was shortlisted, and was scheduled for the Online Assessment.
It was an off campus hiring drive for 2023 grads in specific. Pretty sure I got shortlisted based off my internship. 

##### Online Assessment: 3 Questions, 90 mins
[Question 1](https://leetcode.com/discuss/interview-question/4272374/flipkart-or-OA-2023-or-binary-string)
[Question 2](https://leetcode.com/discuss/interview-question/4415394/FlipkartClearTrip-SHl-SDE-Test-December-17)
Question 3: Given a list of strings, each string consisting of 1s & 0s. Given int X and Y. Find max number of strings you can take such that total count of 1s is less than X and that of 0s is less than Y.

I found the questions slightly difficult, especially because they were worded in a very confusing/poor manner. Managed to pass about 70% test cases overall. 

##### PS/DS Interview 1: 45 mins
No theoretical questions. Introductions and straight into DSA. You are not required to execute code, but to explain all possible approaches in increasing efficiency, write code on whiteboard, debug it, dry run it, and consider the time/space complexity. Refer: Flipkart SDE Interview Guide on their website. 

[Question 1: This](https://leetcode.com/problems/increasing-triplet-subsequence/description/) with a twist: nums[i] < nums[k] < nums[j], for i<j<k. Medium
Question 2: Split the array into N subarrays where each subarray has size 1 or sum at least K. 2 dimensional DP. Medium/Hard

##### PS/DS Interview 2: 1 hour
Question 1: Job Sequencing problem with Deadlines. Medium
[Question 2](https://leetcode.com/problems/shortest-path-visiting-all-nodes/description/): Hard

##### Hiring Manager/Culture Fit Round: 30 mins

Was more of a discussion than interview. Be well prepared so you know what qualities they're looking for, and how to show that you possess those.

# Flipkart Interview Experience for SDE-1 (On-Campus) - FTE

Last Updated : 20 Dec, 2024

## Interview Date: 1st Dec, 2024

Company Name: [Flipkart](https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/companies/flipkart/)

#### On-Campus: IITISM Dhanbad

## Round 1: Coding Round

Duration: 90 minutes

### Questions:

* 2 medium-level problems from LeetCode.
* 1 hard-level problem similar to "Rat in a Maze."

#### Outcome:

* 13 candidates were selected for Round 2.
* 10 candidates were placed on the waitlist for Round 2.

## Round 2: Technical I

The interview began with brief introductions and then transitioned into technical questions:

### Problem 1

* Find the largest length of a subsequence in an array where (max element - min element = 1).
* Used hash maps to solve the problem
* Performed dry runs on four examples provided by the interviewer.
* Discussed time and space complexities for both ordered and unordered maps.

### Problem 2

* Find the element at the nth row and kth index in Pascal's Triangle.
* Explained the intuition and derived the formula due to time constraints.

## Round I: Online Assessment

The assessment consists of three hard level questions based on trees and graphs. I don’t remember the exact questions. I am able to solve only 2 questions, and for the third question, I am able to pass 60% test cases. The questions were not straightforward; they were written in story format and bombarded with too much information on purpose to confuse. One advice for this round is to keep a note of all data you have in the question and what actually needs to be solved, so that you can quickly decide how to solve the problem and what data is needed and by discarding useless data and story, I wasted a lot of time by not doing this, hence was not left with time to optimised my third solution code.

## Round II: Interviews

After the online assessment, I was not very hopeful of receiving the interview call, but after 2 days later I got an email from Flipkart HR that my interviews are scheduled for tomorrow. The mail stated there will be three rounds of interviews, Problem Solving and Data Structures-1(PSDS-1), and based on the results of PSDS-1, my PSDS-2 will be scheduled. If cleared, this will be followed Hiring Manager Round on the next day. The interviews were scheduled on weekends, so there is no clash with my office work while taking the interviews.

### PSDS-1

I was asked one easy and one medium question, and the time duration for the interview is 1 hour. The questions are shared in a Google Doc, and the code is expected to be written in the doc itself, though interviewers are not emphasising maintaining the syntax; they are more focused on knowing the thinking behind arriving at those solutions. The easy question is of dictionary datatype, where I have to tell the element with the maximum occurrence. The medium question is Candy Crush 1D ([link](https://youtu.be/IcyOjlzySXI?si=1sk_i4SSjnFESKWE)). I solved both questions, and 15 minutes later, HR called me to inform me that my PSDS-2 round is scheduled half an hour later on the same day.
